issues.t: Nine-speed automatic failure or slipping into neutral
issues.sym: The van drops into neutral while driving, won't pick up a gear after leaving Park, slips, or loses drive altogether. A transmission service message may appear.
issues.why: The early 948TE nine-speed automatic had enough internal and control problems that FCA extended its warranty on 2015 ProMaster City vans to 6 years or 100,000 miles. Owners also report failed valve bodies and range sensors.
issues.next: If it loses drive, get off the road safely and have it towed. Ask a Ram dealer to check your VIN for warranty extension X80 before paying for a transmission.

issues.t: Harsh, late or erratic shifts from the nine-speed
issues.sym: Jerky or clunky shifts, especially at low speed, delayed downshifts, hunting between gears, or a shudder when pulling away.
issues.why: The nine-speed automatic depends heavily on its control software and learned shift settings. FCA issued several updates to the transmission computer and a relearn procedure to smooth out shifting.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check for transmission software updates and to run the quick learn procedure. Make sure the fluid level is correct before anything else is replaced.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption on the 2.4L
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes with no visible leak, and the low oil pressure light may come on. Running low can damage the engine.
issues.why: FCA traced the problem to how the engine computer cut fuel during deceleration. It extended coverage on 2015-2018 ProMaster City vans built through August 8, 2018 to 7 years or 100,000 miles, with an engine long block replacement if the van fails an oil consumption test.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every fill-up or two and top off as needed. If it uses oil, ask a dealer for the oil consumption test and the XB1 warranty extension.

issues.t: Cooling fan motor wears out and the engine overheats
issues.sym: A whining or grinding fan noise, a check engine light (often a cooling fan code such as P0481), the temperature gauge climbing in traffic, or overheating that needs a tow.
issues.why: Early fan motors used a bushing that was not lubricated well and wore against its shaft. FCA notice V54 covers 2015-2017 vans and replaces the fan module free if it is the older bushing type.
issues.next: Stop driving if the gauge climbs into the red. Ask a Ram dealer whether notice V54 applies to your VIN; the fix is free if it does.

issues.t: Power steering rack can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaking under the front of the van and steering that suddenly takes much more effort.
issues.why: A casting flaw in the hydraulic steering rack housing could crack and let fluid escape.
issues.next: Have a dealer check whether recall U23 has been done. The inspection and any rack replacement are free.

issues.t: ABS module can fail without warning (recall)
issues.sym: ABS or stability control warning lights, or braking and automatic braking that don't work as they should.
issues.why: Some anti-lock brake modules were damaged internally during production.
issues.next: Get the recall done right away. The dealer replaces the ABS module free.

issues.t: Turn signal flash rate doesn't warn of a burned-out bulb (recall)
issues.sym: A turn signal bulb can be out without the dash indicator flashing faster to warn you, so other drivers don't see your signal.
issues.why: The body computer software didn't change the flash rate when a signal failed, which breaks federal lighting rules.
issues.next: Check your turn signals by walking around the van, and have the free body computer update (recall Y71) done.

issues.t: Child seat may not stay locked in by the seat belt (recall)
issues.sym: The seat belt may stop holding a child seat tightly after it has been installed.
issues.why: The automatic locking feature in some seat belt retractors could switch off too early.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect the seat belt retractors and replace them if needed. It's free.

issues.t: Trailer brake lights don't work (recall)
issues.sym: When towing, the trailer's brake lights don't come on when you press the brake.
issues.why: Software in the trailer tow lighting module could stop the trailer brake lights from working.
issues.next: If you tow, have a helper check the trailer lights and ask the dealer to replace the trailer light module for free.

issues.t: Wrong tire pressure and load label (recall)
issues.sym: The label on the door jamb may list the wrong tire pressure, load capacity, seating count or spare size.
issues.why: The tire placard was printed with incorrect information. Overloading or wrong tire pressure can affect handling.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the free replacement label, and use the correct pressure from the dealer until then.

issues.t: Parking brake sticks or won't hold in cold weather
issues.sym: The parking brake freezes on and drags, won't release, or doesn't hold the van on a hill. Rear brakes may wear quickly afterward.
issues.why: Owners report the parking brake cable and rear brake parts freezing or binding, especially in winter.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes and parking brake cables inspected. In freezing weather, use wheel chocks rather than the parking brake if it has been sticking.

issues.t: Brake squeal or grinding
issues.sym: Squealing, scrubbing or grinding from the front or rear brakes, sometimes soon after new brakes.
issues.why: FCA issued service bulletins for front brake noise (new pads and hardware) and rear brake noise (new shoes and wheel cylinders) on early vans.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected. Mention the factory brake noise bulletins so the shop uses the updated parts.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power or limp mode
issues.sym: The engine cuts out or drops to a crawl of about 5-20 mph with warning lights on. Restarting may help for a while before it happens again.
issues.why: Owners report the engine or transmission computer putting the van in a protective limp mode. Causes vary, so the stored trouble codes matter.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Get off the road safely. Have the codes read as soon as possible, before clearing them, so the cause can be found.

issues.t: Oil leak from the oil filter housing or cooler
issues.sym: Oil spots under the front of the van, a burning oil smell, or the oil level dropping.
issues.why: Owners report leaks from the oil cooler and from the oil filter mounting surface on the 2.4L engine.
issues.next: Have the leak cleaned and traced with dye before parts are replaced. Keep the oil topped up in the meantime.

issues.t: Cracked cylinder head needing a new engine
issues.sym: Coolant loss, overheating, white exhaust smoke, misfires, or an engine that runs badly or won't run, often around 80,000 miles.
issues.why: Several owners report cracked cylinder heads on the 2.4L engine that led to full engine replacement after the powertrain warranty ended.
issues.next: If you lose coolant or see the gauge climb, stop and have a cooling system pressure test done before the damage spreads.

issues.t: Clunk at low speed from worn front axle joints
issues.sym: A clunk when pulling away or turning at low speed, or vibration when accelerating.
issues.why: Worn front half shafts, CV joints or tripod joints. FCA has a service bulletin for this noise, and owners report CV replacements around 80,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the front axles checked for play and torn boots. Replace a worn axle before the joint fails.

issues.t: Squeaky or noisy door hinge
issues.sym: A creak or pop when opening or closing a door.
issues.why: A service bulletin covers noisy side door hinges, with replacement only for hinges that have a built-in door check.
issues.next: Try lubricating the hinge first. If the noise returns, ask a dealer about the hinge bulletin.

issues.t: Door handle or latch binds or won't open
issues.sym: An outside door handle that does nothing when pulled, or a door latch that sticks.
issues.why: Service information covers front and cargo door latches and outside handles that stop working or bind.
issues.next: Have the latch and handle checked before the door won't open at all.

issues.t: A/C stops blowing cold
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm air, or cools poorly on hot days.
issues.why: Service cases cover low refrigerant with no obvious leak and a faulty A/C pressure sensor that keeps the compressor from running.
issues.next: Have the A/C pressures and codes checked and do a proper leak test before replacing major parts.

issues.t: Check engine light for small evaporative leak
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0456 (small evaporative emissions leak). The van drives normally.
issues.why: A small leak in the fuel vapor system, often a gas cap, hose or seal. FCA issued a special test procedure for this code.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap clicks tight. If the light returns, have the vapor system smoke tested.

issues.t: Battery drains when parked
issues.sym: The van won't start after sitting, or the battery keeps going dead.
issues.why: A dealer service case covers battery drain on these vans. An aftermarket upfit or accessory left powered can also be the cause.
issues.next: Have the battery tested, then have a shop do a parasitic draw test to find what is pulling power.

issues.t: Dash display hard to read or goes dark
issues.sym: The speedometer and gauges are hard to read in daylight even at full brightness, or the gauge display goes black or stops working.
issues.why: Owners report dim cluster lighting on early vans and instrument displays failing on later ones.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Have the instrument cluster checked if gauges stop working; you need a working speedometer. Check the brightness setting first if it's only dim.

issues.t: Headlight bulbs burn out often
issues.sym: Headlight bulbs fail every few months.
issues.why: Owners report repeated headlight bulb failures. Touching the glass of a new bulb or a poor connection can shorten bulb life.
issues.next: Replace bulbs in pairs without touching the glass, and have the connector and wiring checked if they keep failing.
